claims.claim: PSTN codecs show strong gender bias and neural codecs introduce language bias in the reported analysis.
claims.limitations: Codec set, languages, gender labels, quality measure, and files define the boundary; causal mechanisms and mitigation in deployed networks remain open.

claims.claim: The paper reports relative WER/CER reductions of 4.21% and 5.40% and up to 16.12x real-time speedup over offline adaptation.
claims.limitations: Datasets, elderly populations, prompt clusters, and Whisper versions bound the claim; broader disorders, languages, and online failure recovery remain open.

claims.claim: On NIST SRE 2019 and SITW, the method reports up to 7% relative Cllr reduction versus discriminative linear fusion.
claims.limitations: Datasets, recognizer diversity, score distributions, and calibration protocol bound the result; new speakers, channels, and attacks need separate evaluation.

claims.claim: The paper reports near-perfect explanations for some methods and shows their use in finding spurious correlations.
claims.limitations: Event annotations, task type, explanation method, and proxy definition bound the claim; faithfulness under distribution shift remains open.

claims.claim: The paper reports improved low-resource translation and zero-resource operation, with a small high-resource tradeoff.
claims.limitations: Languages, phoneme recognizer, curriculum, and benchmark define the boundary; zero-resource claims depend on what other language information is available.

claims.claim: The paper reports reliable target-voice conversion on the Single-Word-Production Dutch-iBIDS dataset.
claims.limitations: Single words, EEG setup, target voices, and small dataset define the claim; intelligibility, privacy, consent, and real assistive communication remain open.

claims.claim: The paper presents a systematic evaluation framework intended to guide speech-LLM voice interaction.
claims.limitations: Benchmark tasks, prompts, listeners, model versions, and acoustic measures define the comparison; long-term interaction quality and user adaptation remain open.

claims.claim: The paper reports consistent translation improvements, especially in limited-data languages.
claims.limitations: CVSS, unitizer, schedule, model size, and languages bound the result; naturalness, speaker identity, and unseen domains need separate tests.
